captions.detailed: A track fixie crankset featuring a single forged right crank arm with a five-arm spider, a matching left crank arm, and a black 48T chainring bolted to the spider. The assembly is connected by a central bottom-bracket spindle passing through a cylindrical bottom-bracket shell. Two black rat-trap style pedals are mounted via stub axles at the outer tips of each crank arm, allowing them to spin freely relative to the rotating arms.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of a track bicycle crankset with a central bottom-bracket spindle, a right crank arm with a 5-bolt spider, a left crank arm, a black chainring, and two rat-trap pedals. Ensure the spindle can rotate inside its shell, and each pedal has a revolute joint at the end of its respective crank arm.
captions.factory: Define the bottom-bracket shell using a central Cylinder. Create the spindle as a square-tapered extrusion or stepped cylinder. Model the crank arms by lofting or unioning cylindrical bosses at the spindle and pedal ends with a tapered connecting body. Construct the 5-arm spider on the right arm and bolt a gear-toothed chainring (created via polar patterns of teeth on a flat ring) to it. Model the rat-trap pedals using rectangular plates with small grip protrusions (cleats) arrayed along the edges, joined by a central axle cylinder. Assemble the parts using revolute joints for the main spindle rotation and for each pedal axle.
